props.name: metallic nickel on ceramic cubes (synthesis-gas reactor)
props.description: Catalyst mass of the tubes of the synthesis-gas reactor: ceramic cubes of 0.75 in. covered with metallic nickel.

props.name: active carbon removes poisons
props.statement: Before the synthesis the gas is passed at room temperature through a vessel of active carbon pellets (7 x 10 mm) to remove any Fe(CO)5 formed and other compounds poisonous to the catalyst (COS).

props.name: catalyst choice avoids byproducts
props.statement: In the high-pressure synthesis from CO and H2 the choice of catalyst and reaction conditions is very important to prevent by-product formation.

props.name: co below 20 percent
props.statement: The CO content of the converter inlet gas must be below 20 %, otherwise too many higher alcohols are formed; hence the H2/CO ratio must be much higher than 2 : 1.

props.name: co2 route less exothermic
props.statement: In the synthesis from CO2 and H2 the hydrogen consumption per mol methanol is higher than from CO, but the reaction is much less exothermic, so local overheating of the catalyst mass is more easily avoided.

props.name: cold-gas fraction and exit temperature
props.statement: About 15 % (6000 Nm3/h, 15.5 % of the total gas) of cold synthesis gas is used instead of the about 25 % needed for isothermal operation; with the hot gas entering at 330 °C the exit temperature is about 360 °C (361.5 °C calculated), which is not harmful because the equilibrium approach is small.

props.name: converter cooling needed
props.statement: Methanol formation is exothermic; because the temperature rise shifts the equilibrium unfavourably and increases the unwanted side reactions, the gases in the reactor should be cooled, here by injecting cold synthesis gas between the catalyst zones.

props.name: crude methanol byproducts
props.statement: The crude methanol was assumed, in rough agreement with industrial data, to contain besides methanol dimethyl ether, isobutyl alcohol, a di-isopropyl alcohol and oil (heptene); dimethyl ether is removed by a pre-distillation.

props.name: design conversion 15 % per pass
props.statement: A conversion of 15 % per pass (on CO fed) is the economic optimum: a very high conversion needs so long a contact time that too many by-products form and the reactor becomes too large; a very low conversion gives too large a circulation and pumping cost and a harder separation of crude methanol.

props.name: design H2/CO 3.7 at converter inlet
props.statement: The H2/CO ratio in the converter inlet gas was set at 3.7; in practice 3.5 to 4 is used.

props.name: design pressure 260 atm
props.statement: The working pressure was set at 260 atm, a compromise between the more favourable equilibrium at higher pressure and the larger equipment and compression costs.

props.name: design reaction temperature about 330 °C
props.statement: The reaction temperature of the converter is about 330 °C: at lower temperature the reaction rate is too low; much higher, the equilibrium shifts unfavourably and more by-products form.

props.name: equilibrium constants newton dodge

evidence.note: columns t °C and K; K is 1,5 x 10-3 at 260, 3,1 x 10-4 at 300, 8,7 x 10-5 at 340 and 2,7 x 10-5 at 380 (OCR of the multiplication signs); quote withheld: sha256:6b1e1b7174f11d013f111d83180e1fb8528ab827a647cf408fe42a3904df704e chars:42

props.note: cited from Newton and Dodge (litt. 9, J. Am. Chem. Soc.)
props.statement: Equilibrium constant of CO + 2 H2 -> CH3OH: 1.5 x 10^-3 at 260 °C, 3.1 x 10^-4 at 300 °C, 8.7 x 10^-5 at 340 °C and 2.7 x 10^-5 at 380 °C.

props.name: fresh gas h2 co 2 35
props.statement: The fresh synthesis gas must have an H2/CO ratio of 2.2 to 2.4; the synthesis-gas reactor conditions were calculated for H2/CO = 2.35 in the product.

props.name: gas load 40000
props.note: the gas load is cited from litt. 15 (Winnacker-Weingaertner)
props.statement: The gas load of a methanol reactor working under analogous conditions and with the same catalyst is about 40,000 Nm3/hr per m3 of catalyst; for the 38,830 Nm3/hr of this reactor a catalyst volume of 1 m3 was taken.

props.name: h2 co 4 at 8 10 fold recycle
props.statement: With an 8- to 10-fold gas recycle an H2/CO ratio of about 4 proved very effective.

props.name: heat of methanol formation
props.note: 21600 is printed with the unit kcal/mol, 21,6 kcal on p. 5
props.statement: The heat released in methanol formation is 21600 kcal/mol (as printed); the methanol production is 43.9 kmol per hour, giving a heat release of 950,000 kcal/hr in the reactor.

props.name: high pressure favours conversion
props.statement: Because of the volume decrease of the reaction, high pressure (a few hundred atm) favours the conversion considerably.

props.name: inert gas 13 percent
props.statement: There is an optimum inert-gas (mainly N2) percentage in the recycle gas: a high percentage gives high pumping costs and a less favourable conversion, a low one needs much purge; in practice it is allowed to rise to about 13 %.

props.name: narrow temperature window
props.statement: The temperature range in which the synthesis can be realized is small: well below 300 °C the reaction rate is so small that the reactor capacity becomes very low; above 400 °C the equilibrium becomes unfavourable.

props.name: nh3 o2 injection sulfur
props.statement: Beforehand the gas is injected with 0.5 g NH3 per m3 gas with some O2 to oxidize the sulfur compounds.

props.name: no temperature gradient needed
props.statement: Since equilibrium is far from being approached at both 340 °C and 360 °C (equilibrium approach 22.8 % and 26.6 %), applying an optimal falling temperature gradient over the reactor has no point.

props.name: recycle ratio 9 74
props.statement: The material balance gives a recycle ratio (reactor gas B / fresh feed A, in moles) of x = 9.74.

props.name: design choice: methanol from CO and H2
props.statement: Method A, high-pressure synthesis from CO and H2, was chosen because by-products were not wanted and the aim was only methanol with the lowest possible hydrogen consumption.

props.name: small co2 excess not removed
props.statement: The small excess of CO2 in the synthesis gas does not disturb the methanol synthesis and can also be converted to methanol, so removing it was not considered worthwhile; the amount is too small to justify a CO2 absorption plant.

props.name: zno absorbs sulfur
props.statement: Although the natural gas was assumed sulfur-free, the gas can if needed be passed through a tank of cylindrical zinc-oxide tablets (0.1875 x 0.5 in.) that convert H2S and mercaptans into ZnS.
